title: 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500
shortVersion: This is a ground-up redesign, not a refresh. Two new V8s replace the 5.3 and the 6.2. The trim walk drops from nine names to seven, and LT, RST and LTZ are gone. Every truck gets a 16.3-inch center screen and a 12.2-inch digital cluster. Here is the catch: Chevy has not published horsepower, towing, payload or pricing yet. Specs are due September 17 and pricing September 18. Production starts in October. Order banks are not open yet, so right now all any dealer can do is put you on a list.

blocks.label: What Changed
blocks.heading: Almost everything, including the names.
blocks.sub: If you shopped a Silverado in the last few years, half the trims you knew no longer exist. Start here.

items: A 5.7L replaces the 355-horsepower 5.3L. A 6.6L replaces the 420-horsepower 6.2L. Chevy is calling it the most powerful Silverado ever but has not released a single output figure.
LT, RST and LTZ are gone.
Seven trims now: WT, Custom, Custom Trail Boss, Silverado, Trail Boss, High Country and ZR2.
Order it with 4x4 in the US and the Z71 off-road package comes standard. That is the trim replacing the volume LT and RST business.
A 16.3-inch center display and a 12.2-inch digital gauge cluster are standard, even on a WT. High Country and ZR2 add an 11.5-inch passenger screen and a head-up display.
Super Cruise spreads down the lineup.
More trims can get it than any Silverado before, and it now works while towing.
The four-cylinder was the weak link on paper. The extra gears help.
Two-inch lift, 35-inch tires, front and rear electronic lockers, Multimatic DSSV dampers.

blocks.label: The Lineup
blocks.heading: Seven trims, and only three of them matter to most people.
blocks.sub: Three of the seven ride lifted from the factory. Here is what each one is actually for.

rows.name: WT
rows.desc: Fleet and job site. Vinyl or cloth, steel wheels, nothing decorative. Gets the same 16.3-inch screen and digital cluster as the expensive trims, which is new. Buy it if the truck earns money.

rows.name: Custom
rows.desc: The cheapest one you would drive every day. Body-color trim, alloy wheels, a real interior. This is where a lot of the old LT budget lands.

rows.name: Custom Trail Boss
rows.desc: Custom with the factory lift and off-road hardware. The cheapest way into a lifted Silverado. You give up interior content, not capability.

rows.name: Silverado
rows.desc: New name, and the one I would steer most buyers to. Order it with 4x4 and Z71 comes standard: off-road suspension, skid plates, hill descent. This is the LT and RST replacement, and it is where the money makes the most sense.

rows.name: Trail Boss
rows.desc: Two-inch factory lift and 34-inch off-road tires. Formerly the Trail Boss LT. Good for unplowed side streets and a steep driveway. Expect a firmer ride and worse mileage than a Z71.

rows.name: High Country
rows.desc: 22-inch wheels, real wood, the Multi-Flex console, and the first panoramic sunroof Silverado has offered. Head-up display, rear camera mirror, and Super Cruise standard. It is the loaded one and it will price like it.

rows.name: ZR2
rows.desc: Two-inch lift, 35s, lockers front and rear, Multimatic DSSV dampers, forged carbon fiber inside. A genuinely capable desert and rock truck. It is more truck than a Buffalo winter asks for.

blocks.label: Winter Driving
blocks.heading: Four-wheel drive, and how much of it you need.

items: Four-wheel drive is available across the lineup. The question is what you pair it with. Order the Silverado trim with 4x4 and the Z71 package is standard, which covers off-road suspension, skid plates and hill descent control. For a Williamsville driveway and a lake-effect commute, that is enough truck.

The lifted trims are a different decision. Trail Boss rides two inches higher on 34-inch tires. ZR2 goes to 35s with Multimatic dampers and lockers at both ends. Both are great in deep snow. Both also ride firmer, burn more fuel, and cost more to re-tire. If you are picking between a Trail Boss and a Z71 Silverado for winter, the Z71 is the smarter buy for most people.
Four engines carry into the new truck, two of them brand new. Chevy has not released horsepower or torque for any of them. The displacements below are confirmed. The numbers are not.

cards.small: New V8. Replaces the 5.3L. This will be the volume V8. Output not published.
New V8. Replaces the 6.2L. The big one, on High Country and ZR2. Output not published.
Duramax diesel carries on. Nobody else in the segment offers one. The outgoing version made 305 hp and 495 lb-ft.
TurboMax four, now with a 10-speed. Fine for a daily driver, light for heavy towing.

blocks.label: Availability
blocks.heading: When you can actually get one.
blocks.sub: Every date below traces to GM reporting, not to a press release. Truck timing moves. If any of this changes, I will change the page.

cards.note: Expected to open this fall. Until then, all I can do is put you on the interest list so you are near the front when they do.
Tentative. GM builds the Silverado 1500 at Fort Wayne, Indiana. Launch dates on a new generation slip more often than they hold.
First trucks around year end. Real volume, and real trim and color choice, comes after that. Plan on winter or early spring for a build you actually want.

blocks.label: Pricing
blocks.heading: There is no price yet, and anyone quoting you one is guessing.

items: Chevy has published no MSRP for the 2027 Silverado 1500. Not a starting figure, not a trim walk. Pricing is scheduled to be released September 18, with full specs the day before on September 17. Every number floating around the internet right now is a forecast.

I am not going to put an estimate on my own website and have you hold me to it. When the pricing drops I will post the real trim-by-trim numbers. If you want them the day they land, text me and I will send them to you directly. In the meantime, the only honest price comparison is against a 2026 on the ground, and I can pull those numbers for you today.

blocks.label: My Honest Take
blocks.heading: Three situations, three different answers.
blocks.sub: The new truck is genuinely better. That does not automatically make it your truck this year.

cards.h: You need a truck before winter
cards.body: Buy a 2026. Pricing is published, incentives are on the hood, and dealers want them moved before the new generation lands. It is a truck people have driven for years, with the bugs worked out. You are giving up screens and a new V8, not capability.

Get on the interest list now, because first allocation is small and it goes to whoever is already in line. But do not commit to anything until September 18. Order early, know the number first. Those are not in conflict.

Be honest about how you drive. The 35s, the lockers and the DSSV dampers are real hardware for rock and sand. Around here they mostly cost you ride quality, fuel and tire money. A 4x4 Silverado with Z71 handles a Western New York winter without complaint.

disclaimer: Chevrolet revealed the 2027 Silverado 1500 in June 2026 but has not released horsepower, torque, towing, payload, weights or pricing. Specifications are scheduled for September 17, 2026 and pricing for September 18, 2026. Trim, feature and screen details here come from Chevrolet’s reveal materials. Production and order bank timing comes from GM Authority and GM-Trucks reporting and is subject to change. Any towing or output figure you see elsewhere for the 2027 truck is currently an estimate or a carryover 2026 number. Accurate as of August 27, 2026. Always confirm final specifications and pricing on the window sticker.
